subject: Workplace Skills
title: Context Switching Costs
description: A fast breakdown of Context Switching Costs for builders.

hook.text: Gerald Weinberg estimated that adding a second project cuts productive time to 40% per project, not 50%.

buildup.text: Context switching forces your brain to reload rules, goals, and state. That reload isn't free or instant.

discovery.text: The switching tax is invisible. You don't feel the lost minutes, but they compound across every transition.

twist.text: Three simultaneous projects leave you roughly 20% effective on each. The math argues for serialization.

climax.text: Batch similar tasks into themed blocks. Do all writing Tuesday morning, all meetings Tuesday afternoon.

punchline.text: Batch similar work. Kill the switching tax.

quiz.question: What happens to productivity when you switch between three projects?
options: You remain 33% effective on each project
Roughly 20% effective on each due to switching costs
Productivity is not affected by project count
